wireDescriptor.description: Attach an agent-authored annotation to a symbol in the shared index. Provenance is enforced: `author_class` is hardcoded 'agent' for tool writes (a tool call cannot write a 'human' note), and the row records the caller's self-declared `toolIdentity` plus timestamps. Re-annotating the same symbol+path updates the note in place and reports the note it replaced — one note per author per location is enforced by a unique index over (project, symbol, author, path). The symbol is not checked against the index; the reply MEASURES whether an editor surface can show the note and says so in `surfacing`. `editor` is the JOINT truth the hover and graph badge use: the name (or qualified name) must be indexed AND declared in the resolved file, so a name indexed only in another file is reported `editor: false` with the reason rather than promised. `path` resolves to the index's own spelling, so `src/a.ts`, `./src/a.ts` and the absolute path are the same note. Declared bounds: body 2000 chars, toolIdentity 200 chars, symbol 500 chars, path 1024 chars — refusals, never truncation. Annotations are opinions layered on evidence, never index facts. On a project with no index, the first write creates that project's annotation store and `surfacing.editor` is false. To change source code use bb_edit; to read notes back use bb_annotations.

symbol.description: symbol name to annotate, max 500 chars (`target`/`query` are accepted as aliases); it is not required to exist in the index — reachability is measured and reported

body.description: annotation text, max 2000 chars counted in code points (an astral glyph is one character); empty or whitespace-only is refused

path.description: optional file path to scope the note to one file's copy of the symbol, max 1024 chars; resolved to the index's own spelling (`brain_file.relative_path`), so `src/a.ts`, `./src/a.ts` and the absolute path all reach the same note

toolIdentity.description: optional name of the calling agent/tool, max 200 chars (recorded verbatim; line breaks and control characters are refused)
